monthly_review.summary: You've shifted toward higher-intensity running this month, with faster paces and more time in Zones 3–4, but at the cost of reduced total volume and lower aerobic training effect per run compared to last month.
monthly_review.highlight: Your Zone 4 time jumped from 3% to 21% while Zone 1+2 dropped from 79% to 52%, indicating a significant shift toward threshold/anaerobic work — unusual for a recreational runner without a targeted race build-up.

goal_tracker.message: You need 22.3 more km across 5 remaining sessions (avg 4.5 km/session) to match last month’s volume — achievable with three 5km runs + one 4km + one 3.3km, all at Zone 2 HR ≤138 bpm to rebuild aerobic base.

insights.title: Declining efficiency despite faster pace
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency fell from 13.42 to 13.19 m/sec per bpm, and avg HR rose +8 bpm while pace improved only slightly — suggesting diminishing returns from current intensity distribution; your body is working harder for less physiological gain.

insights.title: Over-reliance on Zone 4 with minimal Zone 5
insights.body: Zone 4 now accounts for 21% of time (up from 3% last month), yet Zone 5 remains at just 3% — meaning most 'hard' efforts are sustained near lactate threshold rather than including true VO2 max intervals or recovery, increasing fatigue risk without peak power stimulus.

insights.title: Cadence-stride trade-off on hard efforts
insights.body: On your fastest recent run (2026-06-04, 7:03/km), stride length surged to 94.69 cm (+23.9 cm vs your monthly avg of 70.7 cm) while cadence held at 149 spm — indicating overstriding under fatigue, which correlates with elevated vertical oscillation (9.2 cm vs monthly avg 7.7 cm).

insights.title: High session density without recovery modulation
insights.body: Three runs on 2026-06-04 (0.5km, 1.0km, 1.0km) totaled only 2.5km but accumulated 7.7 TE — disproportionately high for low volume, likely due to HR spikes (159 bpm on the 7:03/km effort) and inefficient form, reducing recovery capacity before the 11.1km long run 3 days later.

recommendations.action: Replace your next run with a strict 5km Zone 2 session (HR ≤138 bpm, pace ~9:10–9:40/km) focusing on relaxed arm swing and midfoot landing to restore aerobic efficiency.
recommendations.reason: Your June avg aerobic TE (2.4) is below May's (2.7), and Zone 2 time dropped from 43% to 32% — this rebuilds mitochondrial density without adding fatigue.

recommendations.action: Perform one 6 × 90-sec cruise intervals at Zone 3 HR (148–155 bpm) with 90-sec walk/jog recovery — keep cadence ≥152 spm and vertical oscillation <8.0 cm using real-time Garmin metrics.
recommendations.reason: You’re spending 24% of time in Zone 3 but lack structured threshold work; this bridges Zone 2 endurance and Zone 4 stress while reinforcing efficient form under load.

recommendations.action: Add a post-run 3-min barefoot drill circuit (A-skips, straight-leg bounds, heel walks) after your longest run this week to reinforce neuromuscular coordination and reduce ground contact time — your current avg GCT is 312 ms, up from May’s implied ~305 ms based on cadence/stride trends.
recommendations.reason: Increased GCT (+~7 ms) and vertical oscillation suggest reduced leg spring efficiency; neuromuscular drills improve elastic energy return without added cardio load.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish the link between heart rate, pace, and movement economy — prioritizing rhythm, relaxation, and metabolic control over speed or distance.
